title: Banjo and washboard dance hall heard from outside
summary: He listened outside a shack dancehall to banjos, washboard and tub bass and counts it as jazz.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: Yeah, 9 years old, you know. No jazz. But they did have some of the Dixieland music around there, like with the banjo and the washboard, you know. Oh, man, I'd stand on the outside of a little old place, we called it a dancehall, it was just built -- just a shack, really. And they would get into some really -- they knew what was going on, you know. Did a lot of dancing.
That's where you sort of hear the rhythm.
Yeah, everybody dancing, you know. Had a

a couple of banjos and the washboard and took a tub and put a string on it, you know, on a post, they would pull it to make it in tune, pull the post. They'd have one of those, you know. Oh, it was really -- that was jazz. They had something going. They had everybody dancing, that's for sure. And it sounded good to me.
